_comment: WC2026 Round of 32, the last R32 tie. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets Switzerland (who beat Algeria 2-0) in the Round of 16. Routes: Colombia WON Group K (3-1 Uzbekistan, 1-0 DR Congo, 0-0 Portugal; 7 pts, GF 4 GA 1, rating 83) -- organized and defensively strong (GA 1), HELD Portugal 0-0, a moderate but efficient attack. Ghana qualified as a BEST THIRD from Group L (1-0 Panama, 0-0 England, 1-2 Croatia; 4 pts, GF 2 GA 2, GD 0, rating 72) -- a disciplined, low-scoring block that HELD ENGLAND 0-0, blunt in attack (GF 2). Class gap ~11 (83 vs 72) -> Colombia the clear favourite, and the better underlying side (held Portugal, GA 1). KEY texture: two ORGANIZED, low-scoring, defensive sides -> a tight, low-total, cagey tie (1-0/1-1/0-0 shape) with elevated extra-time/penalty risk, NOT an open game. KNOCKOUT CAUTION applied, but REFINED by the Argentina-Cape Verde lesson: Ghana is a PROVEN low block (0-0 England), so keep the DRAW/extra-time tail FAT (draw ~27%, 0-0 ~11%) and do NOT zero out Ghana's attack (they can still nick one; BTTS ~44%, not suppressed to ~0). Colombia favoured to a CONTROLLED low-margin win (1-0/2-0), not a rout. RECAL: first pass sat 6.7 pts BELOW the market on Colombia (48.8 vs 55.6) with Ghana's WIN too high -- applied the don't-fade-the-clear-favourite lesson and lifted COL 1.40 -> 1.55 / trimmed GHA 0.85 -> 0.78, moving the excess out of Ghana's WIN while KEEPING the draw tail (the market itself has a high 27.8% draw, respecting the block). Home = Colombia (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.verdict: The cleanest process hit of the round -- side, margin AND texture all nailed. Colombia advanced as the 71.0% pick, won 1-0 (the SINGLE most likely scoreline at 14.1%), kept a clean sheet (the 45.8% branch), and it was Under 2.5 (58.8%) / BTTS-No (56.4%), exactly the cagey low-total shape I described. This tie is the model working end-to-end: I called it two organized, low-scoring sides -> a tight, controlled Colombia win, and it landed as a textbook 1-0. It also validates the whole knockout-caution + refinement arc: I aligned Colombia UP to the market (don't fade the clear favourite) WHILE keeping the goals texture cautious (low total, BTTS-No, high clean sheet) AND keeping the proven-block draw/ET tail fat (Ghana held England 0-0) without zeroing Ghana's attack. The favourite won in regulation -- the draw/ET tail (27%) simply didn't need to fire this time, but pricing it was still correct. Colombia's class + defence (GA 1, held Portugal) told, and Ghana's blunt attack (GF 2) was shut out as expected.
_postmatch.lesson: The synthesis tie: 'clear favourite vs organized low block' resolves most often as a CONTROLLED 1-0/2-0 win in 90' (not a rout, not a shootout) -- which is exactly what the aligned-up-but-cautious calibration predicted. Confirms the R32 method: (1) align the ADVANCE probability to the market (don't fade the favourite), (2) keep the goals texture conservative in knockouts (BTTS-No, high clean sheet, low total), (3) keep the draw/ET tail fat against a PROVEN block but don't zero the underdog's attack. Colombia 1-0 is that recipe landing perfectly. Completes the Round of 32.
